task.object: Traceability of the fixed 51-state listed pentagon 00112
deliverables: reproducible local discovery and independent word verification

assumptions: original C5, palette {0,1,2,3}, boundary exclusion pattern 00112
proper listed states differ at exactly one coordinate for adjacency
leaf endpoints are forced for any Hamilton path
second-factor traceability does not require its own K to be retained
mathematical_context.domain: fixed 51-state graph only; all cuts of size at most four, then ten-second/two-million-node path discovery

mathematica.existence_evidence: General discrete enumeration is possible; no implementation selected.
mathematica.availability_evidence: backend_inventory.py ReadOrCreate on 2026-10-09: no local executable recorded

sagemath.existence_evidence: General discrete enumeration is possible; no implementation selected.
sagemath.availability_evidence: backend_inventory.py ReadOrCreate on 2026-10-09: no local executable recorded

candidate_implementations: exact standard-library bitset cut enumeration and bounded remaining-degree path discovery
python.existence_evidence: delivered check_small_cuts.py and find_hamilton_path.py; completed exact local runs
python.availability_evidence: Python 3.14.3 inventory live check and successful execution

decision.selection_reason: Small graph and exact local finite certificates: all <=4 cuts need about two seconds; a returned path is checked directly as words.
decision.fallback_reason: Local Mathematica and Sage unavailable; exact Python finite graph computation is sufficient.

execution.command_or_input: python3 check_small_cuts.py 4; python3 find_hamilton_path.py; python3 check_protected_edges.py

result.summary: The fixed graph 00112 has a Hamilton path from 12303 to 13203. The explicit 51-state certificate is checked for distinct complete coverage, legal lists, and single-coordinate adjacency. All cuts of size <=4 satisfy the stronger forced-endpoint necessary bound.

methods: direct enumeration of all proper listed C5 states
compare states to the projection of the frozen two-row seed
exact complete <=4 cut enumeration with fixed-endpoint strengthened bound
bounded local search followed by independent direct word checks of the returned path
explicit comparison with current first-factor protected K
limitations: traceability is proved only for this fixed listed graph
bounded cuts alone do not prove traceability
no original recolouring graph Hamilton search was performed
this path omits three current K edges, so does not directly replace a K-preserving first-factor seed
no such K retention is required when this graph is the second factor B in the constant-source candidate
manuscript and formal MRS records were not changed
